data.name: txtBasics.Text
data.value:
Welcome to Challenge 1. For this challenge, you are assumed to have a basic knowledge of programming; enough to solve common problems.
Upon hitting the start button, a question will appear in the text box above and you will be given a code editor to solve said question.
Once you have finished coding your solution, press "Execute" and the program will compile your code and execute it. If the output is the same as the expected output for that question, you will be awarded the appropriate points depending on time taken: 4 for a "golden" time, 3 for a "silver", 2 for a "bronze", and 1 for all others.
If a question is too difficult, press the "Skip" button. Don't worry, there are more than enough questions for you to attain the minimum score of 15!
If you messed up, and require for the given code to return to its original state, press "Reset".
Don't try cheating, though! A system is implemented which checks that you have used the most suitable methods for the problem at hand, which are provided to you in the other tabs.

data.name: txtStrings.Text
data.value:
Here are some string methods you may find useful:
.Length: Returns length of the string.
.ToLower(): Converts string to lowercase.
.Replace(A, B): Replaces all occurrences of a substring A with another substring B.
Substring(A, B): Extracts a portion of a string, starting from a specific index A and optionally with a specified length B.
Any(char.*): Check if any character in the string meets a condition (like char.IsDigit, char.IsUpper, etc.).
char.IsDigit(): Checks if a character is a digit.
char.IsUpper(): Checks if a character is an uppercase letter.
char.IsSymbol(): Checks if a character is a symbol.
== (Equality Operator): Compares two strings for equality.

data.name: txtArrays.Text
data.value:
Split(A): Splits a string into an array of substrings based on a delimiter A (e.g., "Hello+World".Split('+')).
.Length: Returns the length of the array (i.e., number of elements in the array).
.Average(): Returns the average value of a numeric array (works for int[], double[], etc.).
% (Modulo Operator): Checks for even/odd numbers when applied to numbers in the array using 2 as the operand
+= (Addition Assignment Operator): Adds a value to an existing variable (commonly used for accumulating results, like summing numbers).
.ToArray(): Converts a collection into an array

data.name: txtOthers.Text
data.value:
+= (for strings and arrays): In strings, it appends text to a string; in arrays, it adds elements or accumulates values.
>, <, >=, <= (Comparison Operators): Used for comparing integers, floats, and other types.
.ToString(): Converts numbers or other types into string representation (e.g., int.ToString()).
